clue.text: Building in Toronto we ransacked

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters spanning these three words

parts.note: the end of Toronto, the whole of we and the start of ransacked run together

explanation.surface: Vandals have trashed some building in the Canadian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ransacked' looks like an anagram signal, but it only lends its first letter to the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower is a tall structure, so it is one kind of building.

clue.text: Try in international match

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it sounds like rugby, a try scored in a match; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To test something is to try it out, and a Test is a full international fixture in cricket or rugby.

clue.text: Plant in season, flourishing

parts.note: winter is one of the four seasons
green describes growth that is fresh and thriving

explanation.surface: A plant that thrives during a particular time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintergreen is an evergreen shrub whose leaves give a minty oil, so it is a named plant.

clue.text: Tell the Spanish entering class

parts.note: rate as in first-rate, a grade or class

explanation.surface: An instruction to inform the Spaniards as they join a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell or narrate it.

clue.text: A sonnet mistakenly associated with Michigan state

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is one of the fifty US states, in the upper Midwest.

clue.text: Feisty old lady's protest about limited hearing

clue.text: European entertained by respectable relative

parts.note: nice in the sense of decent or proper

clue.text: What may be worn in the sun to look at fish close to shore?

clue.text: Be indebted to the openers in our winning eleven

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the openers are the first two batsmen; here they are the first letters of the words.

clue.text: Poised in a theatre playing heartless deputy

parts.note: only the first and last letters of deputy remain

explanation.definitionFit: Being at the ready is an idiom for prepared and waiting to act, just as poised.

clue.text: Sleeveless garment: troupe's leader is after one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Is after' reads as wants; in the wordplay it places one piece behind the other.

clue.text: Copper, perhaps, in bar

definitions.meaning: first meaning: copper is an example of a chemical ...

explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry calls copper an element, and the heating bar of an electric fire or kettle is also called its element.

clue.text: Put away in a stable?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' means to consume food, and doing it as a stable animal does is eating hugely.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes eating a very large amount, as horses graze constantly.

clue.text: Berkshire town has space in part of library

parts.note: Reading is a large town in the English county of Berkshire
room in the sense of free space

explanation.definitionFit: A reading room is a quiet area within a library set aside for study.

clue.text: Moor with scar, an antihero

explanation.definitionFit: The brooding hero of Emily Bronte's Wuthering Heights is a classic literary antihero.

clue.text: Wife dropped from golf club's side

clue.text: Dry here at resort, so replenish one's body fluids

clue.text: Hard nut in nasty sort of accident

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

clue.text: Half–hearted, gospeller with member

parts.note: Luke wrote one of the four Gospels
an arm is a limb, or member, of the body

clue.text: Injured butcher, extremely explicit in large sling

clue.text: Furious with papers crossing line

clue.text: Swindler going down? Gracious!

clue.text: Game show

clue.text: Celebrity found no time at the end
